Date       Date
Case Number: 1951 24122023                  24-12-2023                       10-01-2024
Report: Resolution:
Location:       Florida       Region:     Metropolitan   Classification:     Resolved.
It reported the existence of what it considered an aerial abnormality that it saw and
Summary:   Photographed at "10:13" hours on December 23, 2023, from the commune of

Florida, Santiago Metropolitan Region.

The user described the reported sighting as a white light, whose size could not be discerned, but it was indicated that it was visible for 6 to 10 seconds flying from the north towards the northwest by two witnesses.

He then recounted that (sic): "I was observing with my wife through the telescope when, towards the northwest, a light appeared, at first I thought it was a plane."

Description: It was about an airplane, but it was advancing in a zigzag at an incredible speed,
User: From the coastal mountain range to the Andes, it took no more than 6 seconds.
I took a picture, it's distorted by the object's great speed, it wasn't Venus
that was in the same quadrant, it was obscured by clouds. To the east,
more or less in the direction of Cerro La Cruz, it disappeared."

Along with the report, the file "20231223_221258.jpg" was entered, which is displayed below.

In Figure 1, along with an enlarged detail of the object under study.
                                                     Figure 1

The user's location was georeferenced at coordinates 33° 32' 26" S, 70° 34' 04" W, and 663 m.s.n.m. (Figure 2)

Investigation:

                                                     Figure 2
 The image supporting the report was perused through ELA (Error Level Analysis) and CMF (Copy and Motion Forgery) analysis, confirming its

digital integrity. The analysis of the information contained in its metadata
defined that captured using the ultra-wide angle camera of a Samsung
cellphone, model Samsung Galaxy Note 20 (SM-N980F), at 22:13 (HL) on
December 23, 2023. The machine automatically adjusted with a slow shutter
speed (1/4 s) and the maximum aperture of the lens used (F2.2).

Figure 3

Figure 3 shows the astronomical horizon at the time the image was taken.

1951-1. The most notable elements were the Moon at an azimuth of +14º 29’ and an
apparent altitude of 32º 18’, and the planet Jupiter at an azimuth of +351º 33’ and an
altitude of 43º 50’.

Given the possibility that the reported sighting was related to these astronomical
bodies and considering that, according to the user's testimony, the sighting was
associated with a telescopic visualization, cooperation was requested from the
advisor and head of the Standards and Development Office (DASA) and an
astrophotographer.

The aerospace analysis between 22:00 and 22:30 hours found none that
could account for the luminous record of the case.

The air traffic study at the time of the photographic capture revealed the
existence of at least three aircraft to the north and near the user: the LAN641
and LAN591 flights of LATAM Airlines, and the SKU2804 of Sky Airline. Figure 4
shows their relative positions to the user and to the radial of Jupiter and the
Moon.

Figure 4. Air traffic situation at the time of taking the photograph of the case.

The two LATAM flights followed similar routes to land at Arturo Merino Benítez Airport (SCEL) in Santiago, crossing at 350º radial.

The angle of exposure of their wing surfaces and white fuselages to the Moon, along with the orientation they presented for a few seconds to the observer, would allow them to be associated as a single bright object with rapid and discontinuous movements before disappearing from sight.

Their navigation data at the time of the image are as follows:

a) LAN641, from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC) in Lima, Peru to Arturo Merino Benítez Airport (SCEL). Airbus 240-214, registration PR-TYK. Altitude of 14,250 feet (4,343 m), speed of 376 knots (696 km/h), heading 178°. Coordinates -32.54551° and -70.82404°.

b) LAN591, from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC) in the Dominican Republic to Arturo Merino Benítez Airport (SCEL). Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, registration CC-BGN. Altitude of 8,775 feet.

(2.675 m), speed of 291 knots (538 km/h), on course 178°.
Coordinates -32.87971° and -70.81249°.

The advisor indicated that the movement or shift of the light focus is not the
same as that of the Moon and clouds, and that, together with the fact that the
nearby blue lights near the scene's house appear static, leads him to lean
towards the object under study as the one circulating. He noted that apparently
at the beginning of the trajectory its light trail was smaller than at the end.

What apparently resulted in an increase in the magnitude of its lighting.

He finally added that the length of the plasma trace depended on the time of the photographic exposure.

Additionally, he explained that considering the sunset in Santiago for that day was at 20:55 and the event time was 22:13, it allowed for what was captured to be the flash of a high-orbit satellite, which disappeared as it entered the Earth's shadow cone.

According to the analysis of the testimony and the results of the geographical, forensic, photographic, astronomical, and aerial and aerospace traffic studies, along with the considerations of the consulted specialized advisor, it was concluded that the object appearing in the case photo was the reflection of the Airbus 240-214 aircraft's fuselage and wings, which was ending its LAN641 flight.
Latam Airlines originating from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC) in Lima and landing at Arturo Merino Benítez Airport (SCEL) in Santiago.
